get.description: How one may log in (for the login page).

Off to the identity provider; it sends the browser back to
``/api/auth/oidc/callback``. With ``link``, the university login is
linked to the account logged in now instead (whatever its name).
Back from the identity provider: log the person in.

delete.description: Unlink one's account from the university login (the password stays).

post.description:
Change one's password (the current one is needed); other devices are
logged out, this one stays logged in.

put.description: Remember that the person has seen a tutorial hint.

post.description:
A new item; if one of its identifiers is known among the items the
person can see, the existing item (200).

get.description:
Items the person can read, newest first; ``before`` = last ``id`` for
the next page. ``library`` shows one library only. ``sort=recent``:
by the latest of the item's last change and the reader's last opening,
newest first, paged with ``offset`` instead of ``before``;
``sort=opened``: only items the reader opened, by when.

``trashed=true`` lists the trash instead. ``unsorted=true``: only papers
with a PDF whose details could not be found (all guessed from the file;
papers still being read, and notes or other files without a DOI to
find, are left out). ``tag`` (repeatable: items
with all of them) and ``collection`` (with its subcollections unless
``nested=false``) filter the list, and ``title`` to items with all of its
words in their title (any case). ``X-Total-Count`` is the number of
matching items, for showing the total while paging.
``since=N`` is for syncing:
every item changed after change number N, trashed or not, in change
order; ``limit`` and ``before`` do not apply. The ``Last-Change`` header
is the number to pass as ``since`` next time.

post.description: Another version of an item, e.g. the published one of a preprint.
Cite this version, whatever its kind.

put.description:
Replace the manual edits to the metadata for citing.

Fields set here win over every version's metadata and survive new
lookups; ``null`` hides a field. Needs ``If-Match`` with the ETag from the
last read, so concurrent edits are not lost (412 if the item changed).

delete.description: Move to the trash; restorable with ``POST …/restore``.

put.description:
Give the item to another owner the person may add to: share it with a
group, or take a group's paper for oneself (members may delete it
anyway). Tags and collections of the group that gave it up come off.
Star the paper (for the person only; any paper they can see).

post.description: Remember that the person opened the item (for their recent papers).

get.description:
Papers the person can see that share an identifier or a file with
this one: candidates for merging.
What merging this paper into ``into`` would move and leave behind.

post.description:
Merge this paper into another one (the same paper twice). Needs the
right to change this one; what may move to the other depends on the
person's rights there (see docs/permissions.md).

get.description:
The item in a library the person can read that already has a file
with this SHA-256 (hex), so a client can skip uploading it again; 404 if
there is none.

post.description:
A new item from a file, titled after the file until its text tells more.

The background job looks for a DOI or arXiv ID in the file and replaces
the placeholder metadata (see ``paperus.identify``). A file that is
already in a library the person can read makes no new item: the answer
(200, ``existing``) names the item that has it. ``library_id`` (the
owner): the person's default if not given.
Upload to the item's preferred version.

delete.description: Move to the trash; restorable with ``POST …/restore``.

get.description:
Passages for ``q`` in the libraries the person can read (or one
``library``): its words (quotes for phrases, ``-`` to exclude), its
meaning, or both; ``type`` (repeatable, CSL types) limits the items.
``per_item`` keeps the best few per paper or note, so more papers fit;
``item`` searches within one paper. The ``X-Search-Mode`` header says
what was used: without the ML service, hybrid search falls back to
keywords.

Citations for the given papers (``item``, repeatable), a collection
(with its subcollections unless ``nested=false``) or, with neither,
everything the person can read. ``download=true`` offers it as a file
(``.bib`` or ``.json``).

Notes the person can read, last changed first: all of them, those
about a paper (``item``) or in a collection (with its subcollections
unless ``nested=false``); ``trashed=true`` lists the trash instead.
``X-Total-Count`` is the number of matching notes.

post.description:
A new note for the given owner (or the person's default owner), about
the given papers, optionally put into a collection.

get.description: The note with its text; the ``ETag`` goes into ``If-Match`` when saving.

patch.description:
Save the text. Needs ``If-Match`` with the ETag the editor started
from: 412 if someone else saved in between (then reload and merge).

put.description:
Say the note is about the paper (at a page); changes the page if it
is linked already.

Give the note to another owner the person may add to. Collections of a
group that no longer owns it let it go.

get.description: Earlier texts of the note, newest first.
The note as a Markdown file.

post.description:
Put notes into a collection; those it may not hold (a group's
collection holds only the group's notes) or unknown ones are skipped.

get.description: The person's imports, newest first.

post.description:
Import an export: BibTeX, RIS or CSL-JSON, alone or zipped with its
files. Everything new belongs to ``library_id`` (default: the person's
default owner). Runs in the background; poll ``GET /api/imports/{id}``.

The two are different papers: do not suggest them again (for everyone
who sees both). Needs the right to change at least one of them.

delete.description:
Delete for good everything in the trash the person may change: their
own and that of groups where they are a member or admin.

get.description: How full the storage is (for the bar at the bottom of the menu).

put.description:
Save settings. A new embedding model must be one the ML service
offers; the library is then re-embedded in the background, while keyword
search keeps working and search by meaning covers more and more.

post.description:
Time a model on this installation's ML service with sample passages.
A model not downloaded yet starts downloading: the answer then says
``loading``; ask again in a while.

delete.description: Remove a downloaded model from the ML service (not the one in use).

post.description:
Start a sweep now: ``embeddings`` (embed what is missing), ``text``
(read files still pending), ``text-all`` (read every file again),
``trash`` (delete what is older than the trash days), ``integrity``
(check stored contents), ``integrity-deep`` (also their SHA-256) or
``integrity-clean`` (check and remove unused stored contents).

get.description: The last integrity check's report (None before the first).
What the Authentication settings show besides the settings.

put.description: The university login's client secret; never sent back.

post.description: Whether the identity provider answers at this address.

delete.description: Log everyone out on every device, except this one.

get.description:
The tags of the libraries the person can read, with how they are used
(items in the trash do not count).

post.description: A tag not on any item yet (409 if the library has one of that name).

Tag an item with its owner's, the person's or one of their groups' tag
(see ``Access.may_tag``); the tag is created if that owner has none of
that name (any case), which for a group needs member rights there.

patch.description:
Rename a tag everywhere (409 if another tag of its owner has that
name), set its colour or description, or give it to another owner.

delete.description: Remove a tag from every item and delete it.

get.description:
The collections of the libraries the person can read, flat;
``parent_id`` gives the tree.

patch.description:
Rename, describe or move a collection (not into itself), also into
another library the person may change.

delete.description: Delete a collection and its subcollections; items stay in the library.

get.description:
Before moving a collection into another library: how many of its
papers are not in that library yet.

put.description: Pin the collection to the person's sidebar (readers may too).

post.description:
Add items; those the collection may not hold (a group's collection
holds only that group's items) or the person cannot read are skipped.

get.description: The libraries the person can read: their own first, then their groups'.

put.description: Where new items go unless another library is chosen.

get.description:
The groups the person belongs to (directly or through a group above);
site administrators see every group. Flat; ``parent_id`` gives the tree.

post.description:
A group with its library. Top-level groups: site administrators only,
with a first admin. Subgroups: the parent's admins (who are then admins
of the subgroup too).

delete.description:
Delete an empty group: no groups inside and no items or notes (not
even in its trash). Its tags, collections and memberships go with it.

get.description: Everyone in the group: given a role here or in a group above.

put.description:
Add someone to the group, or change their role here. A role lower than
one inherited from a group above has no effect (inherited roles win).

delete.description: Remove someone's membership here (inherited ones stay).

post.description:
Leave a group one was added to. Membership through a group above can
only be left there.

get.description:
People to add to a group, by username; for site administrators and
group admins.

post.description: A new account (with its private space); 409 if the name is taken.

patch.description:
Reset a password, grant or take admin rights, (de)activate. The last
active administrator cannot lose those rights, and nobody deactivates
themselves.

post.description: Queue a backup now (the worker writes it); 409 if one is running.
The first administrator, logged in right away.

Restore a backup from the backup folder into the empty database; then
people log in with their accounts from the backup.
A token acting as you, narrowed to its scopes (and owners).

BackupConfig.title: BackupConfig
BackupConfig.description: When backups run on their own (checked every hour by the worker).

CollectionChange.title: CollectionChange
CollectionChange.description:
Only the fields given are changed; ``parent_id: null`` moves to the top.

``library_id`` gives the collection, with the collections inside it, to
another library the person may change, e.g. from their own to a group
or back (members may delete a group's collections anyway). It lands at
the top level there unless ``parent_id`` names a collection there.
Papers a group's collection may not hold leave it, unless
``add_papers`` puts them into the group.

FileSource.title: FileSource
FileSource.description: Where a file came from; matters for sharing rules.

MovePreview.title: MovePreview
MovePreview.description: What moving a collection (with those inside) into a library does.

RestoreCheckOut.title: RestoreCheckOut
RestoreCheckOut.description:
Where the backup's files would come from. Files are stored by their
SHA-256, so one already in the storage is the very same file: nothing
is overwritten, missing ones are copied back, extra ones stay.

Role.title: Role
Role.description: What a member may do in a group (and every group inside it).

TagChange.title: TagChange
TagChange.description: Only the fields given are changed; ``null`` clears colour or description.

TagColor.title: TagColor
TagColor.description: Colours a tag can have; the website gives each a light and dark shade.

TagSource.title: TagSource
TagSource.description: Who put a tag on an item (Zotero keeps manual and automatic apart).

VersionIn.title: VersionIn
VersionIn.description:
A version by DOI (metadata is looked up) or with metadata typed in.

Examples: ``{"doi": "10.1038/…"}``; meeting notes:
``{"metadata": {"type": "document", "genre": "Meeting notes",
"title": "Group meeting", "issued": {"date-parts": [[2026, 11, 4]]}}}``.
